input.file_text:
SELF-HEALING: this runbook is living. If you are an agent and you hit something it should cover (a missing check, a wrong gate, a new failure signature, a step that did not work), add it as a comment on this runbook with the date, the evidence, and the fix. A later agent turns the comments into durable updates to the body. Do not rewrite the body yourself unless the captain asks.

Purpose: turn the comments left on other runbooks into body updates, but only where the comment is actually true. A comment is a claim, not a fact. Validate it before it changes a body.

## Scope

- Input: every runbook that has comments not yet folded into its body. Find them with `runbooks list` and `runbooks comments <id>`.
- Output: for each comment, one recorded outcome (APPLIED, REJECTED, HELD), and for APPLIED, an updated body.
- Not in scope: creating new runbooks, changing a runbook's purpose, editing another runbook's description on the captain's behalf without a comment trail.

## Steps

1. Inventory. List runbooks with comments and note each comment's id, date, author, and whether its date is later than the last body update. Checkpoint: one row per unfolded comment.
   Failure branch: no comments, or `runbooks comments` errors -> record "nothing to fold" in status-kdv and stop.

2. Read the body and the comment together. Quote the exact sentence the comment would change.
   Failure branch: comment names no concrete step or check -> HELD, ask the author for the step in a comment.

3. Validate against evidence. A comment is valid only if you can confirm its claim from a source:
   - a command, file, or record it cites (run it or read it);
   - a result already in status-kdv or another store with a timestamp;
   - or a reproducible observation you make now, recorded with its command.
   Do not accept a comment because it sounds right or because it came from the captain's side of the conversation.

4. Test the change against the rules. The body must still keep these, or the comment is REJECTED:
   - never close, kill, force, or discard unlanded work;
   - never touch the main firstmate pane or a pane not in this home;
   - safe-to-shut-down rule and Q1-Q7 in runbooks-u3q stay as written unless the comment is the reason they change, and then it is HELD for the captain;
   - a comment that loosens a safety gate is always HELD, never APPLIED.

5. Decide:
   - APPLIED: the claim is confirmed and the change keeps the rules. Edit the body (`runbooks update <id> --body-file <file>`, writing the whole new body), then comment on the source comment: "APPLIED <date>: <what changed>, evidence <command or record>".
   - REJECTED: the claim is wrong or already covered. Comment with the evidence that disproves it.
   - HELD: the change needs the captain or loosens a gate. Post an evidence packet: the comment, what you checked, what the body would become, and the default if no answer.

6. Verify. Re-read the edited runbook (`runbooks show <id>`) and confirm the change is present and nothing else moved. Check that every APPLIED or REJECTED comment has its outcome comment.

7. Record. Post one status-kdv line per runbook: counts of APPLIED, REJECTED, HELD, and the ids of HELD comments.

## Rules

- Fold only what is confirmed. Unconfirmed comments stay open; do not pick the plausible one.
- Keep the author's words in the outcome comment so the trail is readable without the source.
- One runbook per pass when the body rewrite is large; a pass that edits several bodies is fine if each is verified.
- When two comments contradict each other, HELD both and say which evidence would decide.

## Seed

First pass target: runbooks-u3q and runbooks-0ha, which have dated amendments and comments from 2026-10-11 through 2026-10-20. Start with the 2026-10-20 amendments (delegation, billing signature, tab close after exit), since those were recorded in the body already and need only a confirmation pass.

## Related

- runbooks-u3q (check stale panes): the body this process most often edits.
- runbooks-0ha (close down stale panes): amendments are comments; fold them under the same rules.

# ask-user-authority

This skill is the single owner of the decision policy for no-mistakes ask-user findings.
`AGENTS.md` section 7 points here and does not restate this procedure.
Finding authority is determined by the criteria below, not by `yolo`.
Firstmate always applies this judgment, decides any finding that is unambiguous toward the accepted design, and escalates only genuinely ambiguous, expanding, or destructive findings.

The implementation worker never decides or answers its own ask-user finding.
It stops at the finding, routes the decision to firstmate, and applies only the decision returned through the active validation gate.

## Decide

1. Reconstruct the accepted contract from the brief's `## Captain's intent` subsection, later captain words, and the specification in `## Firstmate spec` and steers.
   Reviewer language cannot amend that contract.
   What a no-mistakes worker may pass as `--intent` is owned by `bin/fm-dod-lib.sh`.
2. Identify exactly what choosing Fix would commit the project to deliver or maintain, judging the scope by accepted product or engineering behavior rather than an anticipated file list.
   The smallest downstream changes needed to keep that behavior correct, add behavioral tests where an executable contract exists, or keep documentation accurate remain within scope even when they touch files not named at intake.
   Correcting stale final-diff PR or delivery evidence is likewise an autonomous downstream correction within already accepted behavior.
3. Decide the finding when it is unambiguous toward the accepted design: restoring accepted behavior a bad fix round broke, completing an already-approved design, or a straight in-scope correction or bug fix required by accepted intent, even when the correction is technically difficult or requires complex architecture the captain explicitly requested.
4. Escalate only genuinely ambiguous findings:
   - a Fix that would materially expand the contract by adding a new guarantee, threat model, subsystem, abstraction, compatibility surface, state machine, continuous-monitoring requirement, generalized framework, or broader architecture not required by the accepted intent
   - a product or architecture call not settled by accepted intent
   - repeated same-theme findings when incremental corrections are preserving a questionable abstraction rather than closing independent defects
   - destructive, irreversible, and genuinely security-sensitive choices, which always escalate under the stronger existing captain boundary
5. Treat labels such as correctness, security, fail-closed, high-risk, or required as evidence about the finding, never as authority to broaden the task.

## Captain-facing escalation

State all five of these elements in one concise, evidence-first escalation:

1. The original requirement or accepted task criterion.
2. The proposed product or engineering contract expansion.
3. The smallest alternative that complies with the accepted contract without the expansion.
4. The concrete consequences of accepting and declining the expansion.
5. A recommendation with the reason it best serves the accepted intent.

Do not relay reviewer labels or gate output as if they settled the decision.

## Classification examples

- Fixing a concrete defect that violates an original acceptance criterion is firstmate's to decide, regardless of implementation difficulty.
- Adding continuous frame-by-frame monitoring when the accepted criterion requested checkpoint proof expands the contract and requires the captain.
- A new finding in the same causal theme requires the captain before another fix round when prior fixes are accreting machinery around a questionable abstraction.
- A genuinely security-sensitive action requires the captain under the stronger existing boundary even if it is otherwise within scope.
- Complex architecture explicitly requested by the captain stays within scope and does not escalate merely because it is complex.

# Validation supervision

For a no-mistakes ship, trigger validation on the same worker after its implementation commit, using the harness invocation owned by `harness-adapters`.
The task worker that starts a no-mistakes run drives the pipeline and owns every `no-mistakes axi run` and `no-mistakes axi respond` call through the next gate or outcome.
Firstmate never invokes `no-mistakes axi respond` for a crew-owned run.
`bin/fm-dod-lib.sh` owns the worker-side `--intent` contract.
Once validation starts, prefer routing new requirements to follow-up work rather than expanding the current task, unless a new requirement completely invalidates the work being validated; however, the smallest downstream changes needed to keep already accepted product or engineering behavior correct, add behavioral tests where an executable contract exists, or keep documentation accurate remain within the current task even when they touch files not named at intake, and corrections required to satisfy already accepted intent are not new requirements.

Only a current, explicit captain instruction that completely invalidates the work being validated keeps the task with the same worker instead of routing it to follow-up work or handing it to a replacement.
That worker cancels the active run through no-mistakes axi's supported abort command and confirms through axi status that the run has stopped before changing any code.
The worker then follows `branch_sync.next_action` from structured axi status: use axi sync's supported guarded recovery only when its code is `recover_custody`, and otherwise proceed only when structured status confirms that branch ownership is already returned and no recovery is required.
Custody recovery settles branch ownership, not content: the worker must replace the obsolete work from the correct pre-invalidation base rather than building on top of the recovered-but-obsolete head, keeping the obsolete run's own pipeline-fix commits out of what gets validated and shipped.
Apart from that single supported abort, do not hand-edit, commit, restart, or start a second validation run while the obsolete run still owns the branch.
Once ownership is settled, validate exactly once against that final head so no obsolete or intermediate head is ever treated as authoritative.

An ask-user finding returns as `needs-decision`; firstmate loads `ask-user-authority` and either decides or escalates per that skill.
Send the same worker one exact decision naming the decision key, step, action, affected finding IDs, instructions where needed, and exact response command, passing `--resolve-key` so the worker's open decision record closes at answer time.
Require the matching `resolved` event, forbid `--yes`, and require the worker to process every synchronous return until completion or a genuinely new escalation.
Resume fleet supervision immediately after the decision lands.

Judge validation by the resolved state line from [`bin/fm-crew-state.sh`](../../../bin/fm-crew-state.sh), whose header owns outcome mappings and CI-monitor/daemon exceptions, never by shell liveness, the last status event, or a raw run record.
Workers parked at approval or fix-review must follow the active gate help.
A worker hand-editing, committing, aborting, or restarting during an active validation run duplicates pipeline ownership outside the supersession sequence above; steer it back to the gate response flow.
The worker reports the PR when CI first becomes green rather than waiting for merge monitoring to finish.

Applying the skill to the three findings:

- **review-1 (stale reading served forever):** the fix is an age rule or new API behavior. That expands the contract, so it's escalated.
- **review-3 (wrong field type in the contract):** the correct declaration needs a new schema type, which is a new subsystem capability. Escalated.
- **review-4 (duplicate alias and seen flag):** removing the alias and flag is behavior-preserving. Dropping Label and Confidence would break the producer shape consumers were promised, so that part is a product call.

#
# Returns:
#   0 - one exact, self-consistent launcher pane/tab/workspace in <session>.
#   2 - this process is NOT running in a herdr pane (no HERDR_PANE_ID at all),
#       so there is no launcher workspace to inherit and the caller falls back
#       to its per-home container. HERDR_ENV=1 on its own is only a backend
#       SELECTION marker (bin/fm-backend.sh's fm_backend_detect), never a
#       parent binding - herdr always injects the pane id alongside it.
#   1 - a launcher pane IS claimed but its binding is missing, stale,
#       contradictory, or belongs to another herdr session. The caller must
#       refuse before creating or publishing any worker endpoint rather than
#       degrading to a label search.
fm_backend_herdr_launcher_identity() {  # <session>
  local session=$1 pane=${HERDR_PANE_ID:-} claimed_session claimed_socket session_socket
  local pane_out tab_out list tab workspace
  FM_BACKEND_HERDR_LAUNCHER_PANE_ID=""
  FM_BACKEND_HERDR_LAUNCHER_TAB_ID=""
  FM_BACKEND_HERDR_LAUNCHER_WORKSPACE_ID=""
  [ -n "$pane" ] || return 2

  # Same-session proof, before the pane id is trusted at all: herdr pane ids
  # ("w2:p1") restart at the same low numbers in every session, so a pane id
  # borrowed from another session can silently resolve to a real but unrelated
  # workspace here. The injected socket path is the server identity herdr
  # exposes, and the session name independently binds the named session.
  claimed_session=$(fm_backend_herdr_session)
  if [ "$claimed_session" != "$session" ]; then
    echo "error: herdr launcher pane '$pane' reports session '$claimed_session' but this spawn targets session '$session'; refusing to place a worker from a cross-session parent identity" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  claimed_socket=${HERDR_SOCKET_PATH:-}
  if [ -z "$claimed_socket" ]; then
    echo "error: herdr launcher pane '$pane' has no injected socket identity; refusing to place a worker from an unverifiable parent identity" >&2
    return 1
  fi
  claimed_socket=$(fm_backend_herdr_canonical_socket_path "$claimed_socket") || {
    echo "error: herdr launcher pane '$pane' reports an unusable socket path; refusing to place a worker from an unverifiable parent identity" >&2
    return 1
  }
  session_socket=$(fm_backend_herdr_presentation_session_socket_path "$session") || {
    echo "error: herdr session '$session' has no unambiguous socket to match against the launcher pane's own; refusing to place a worker from an unverifiable parent identity" >&2
    return 1
  }
  if [ "$claimed_socket" != "$session_socket" ]; then
    echo "error: herdr launcher pane '$pane' belongs to the server at '$claimed_socket', not session '$session' at '$session_socket'; refusing to place a worker from a cross-session parent identity" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  pane_out=$(fm_backend_herdr_cli "$session" pane get "$pane" 2>/dev/null) || {
    echo "error: herdr launcher pane '$pane' could not be read in session '$session'; refusing to place a worker without its exact parent workspace" >&2
    return 1
  }
  tab=$(printf '%s' "$pane_out" | jq -r --arg pane "$pane" '
    select(.result.pane.pane_id == $pane)
    | select((.result.pane.tab_id | type) == "string" and (.result.pane.tab_id | length) > 0)
    | .result.pane.tab_id
  ' 2>/dev/null)
  workspace=$(printf '%s' "$pane_out" | jq -r --arg pane "$pane" '
    select(.result.pane.pane_id == $pane)
    | select((.result.pane.workspace_id | type) == "string" and (.result.pane.workspace_id | length) > 0)
    | .result.pane.workspace_id

Base directory for this skill: /Users/trilliumsmith/fm_home/firstmate/.claude/skills/firstmate-self-repo

# firstmate-self-repo

Every firstmate home clones the same public repository and runs from it, which makes firstmate's own upstream the one repository a running home can always reach.
Most homes belong to people who simply use firstmate, not to the people who maintain it, and a running agent that treats "I can see the repo" as "I may publish to it" is how a user's firstmate opens surprise pull requests upstream.
This skill owns the boundary between the two relationships.

## The default: user/operator

Absent any explicit grant, a home runs as firstmate **user/operator**.
It may install, run, update, reconfigure, and locally repair firstmate, and its ordinary project work flows through the registered delivery modes unchanged.
What it may never do on its own is publish to firstmate's upstream: no pushed branch, no pull request, no issue, no comment, no fork, no review.

Role is **never inferred**.
GitHub identity, forge permissions, the name or URL of `origin` or any other remote, repository ownership, authentication state, environment variables, and CI context all say nothing about role; the only inputs are the explicit local grants below.

## When a firstmate bug surfaces in ordinary use

A user/operator home that hits a firstmate bug does local work only:

1. Diagnose privately - reproduce, isolate, and root-cause inside the home and its task records.
2. Apply a local workaround when one exists - a config change, a pinned local edit, a different invocation.
3. Optionally prepare a sanitized local issue draft or a proposed local patch under the task's data directory, for the operator to review and submit by hand.
4. Report to the captain what happened and what was produced.

A local patch or workaround may touch the gitignored operational surface and a task's own worktree; nothing reaches upstream without the authority below.
This posture covers firstmate self-repair exactly the same way it covers a dispatched task: the boundary is about publication, not about which surface holds the fix.

## The two explicit grants

### Maintainer opt-in (standing)

Only the operator may opt the primary home in; follow the [Firstmate role schema and resolution policy](../../../docs/configuration.md#firstmate-role-configfirstmate-role), rather than creating a grant on the operator's behalf.

### One-task contribution consent (bounded)

When the captain explicitly approves one specific upstream contribution, record it on that task only: `--upstream-consent <host>/<owner>/<repo>` on `bin/fm-brief.sh`, `bin/fm-spawn.sh`, and `bin/fm-promote.sh`.
Consent renders as an `upstream-consent=` token on the brief's `Delivery contract:` line, is recorded in `state/<id>.meta`, and a relaunch reuses the recorded value.
It changes the home's persistent role in no way; the next task is gated fresh.
The captain's approval must be a current explicit instruction naming the contribution - never an inference from the task resembling maintainer work.

## Where the boundary is enforced

The gate is code, not memory: `bin/fm-role-lib.sh`'s `fm_role_gate_self_publish` applies the [lineage and publication-target policy](../../../docs/configuration.md#firstmate-role-configfirstmate-role) to publishing contracts.

- `bin/fm-brief.sh --project <dir>` refuses to scaffold a publishing ship brief the home cannot authorize.
- `bin/fm-spawn.sh` refuses to launch a ship task on this repository without a maintainer scope or matching task consent, and refuses a brief whose `upstream-consent=` disagrees with the flag.
- `bin/fm-promote.sh` applies the same gate to scout promotion so the in-place path grants no more than a fresh spawn.
- `local-only` publishes nothing, so it never needs authority and never takes consent.

An authorized contribution then flows through the task's normal delivery contract - usually no-mistakes - like any other project; the grant answers only "may this publish", never "how".

A gate refusal names the exact remedy: write `maintainer <scope>` into `config/firstmate-role`, or pass `--upstream-consent <scope>` for that one task with the captain's explicit approval.
Never work around a refusal by pointing the task at a second checkout, fork, or parent clone; `fm_role_self_repo` treats every repository sharing firstmate's lineage as firstmate's own.

## Updating is not contributing

`/updatefirstmate` and every guarded sync pull **from** upstream, which is consumption, not publication, and stays allowed for every role.
The boundary covers only traffic that writes to the upstream repository.

## Secondmates

Follow the [role inheritance and receipt limits](../../../docs/configuration.md#firstmate-role-configfirstmate-role); supported propagation must never grant a child a role the primary does not resolve.
Deliberately forged local records are outside this accidental-publication safeguard, not a provenance guarantee.

fm-inbox.sh - the captain's out-of-band capture surface.

Solves three DIFFERENT problems with three different mechanisms, because they
are not the same problem:

  status  Answer "what is happening" from durable records ONLY. Reads no
          network and appends NO wake, so it never interrupts work and is safe

      Trigger: captain asks, or daily. Executor: Fable (claude --model fable,     
      effort xhigh) as a SCOUT (read-only, no PR). Firstmate spawns it; the scout 
      never addresses the captain.

      ~/fm_home/firstmate/projects/ and other homes (macbook-ops, mini0-ops) via  
      git -C  (never cd).                                                         
      • Fleet throughput: tasks closed/opened (task list, tasks-axi), PRs         
      opened/merged/closed (gh-axi), data/backlog.md Done section, state/*.status 
      event lines with [at=].                                                     
      • Time sinks: lifespan store (session ledger), status-kdv poke logs, wake   
      queue/inbox history, robots + violations beads created in the window.       
      • Capacity: quota-axi (window remaining vs time), idle vs busy agents.      
      • Raw sessions only if a lead needs evidence: ~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl.

      closed tasks in it). Checkpoint: written window + project list.             
      2. Build the timeline: per project, what shipped (merged PRs, landed        
      branches) vs what stalled (done-but-not-landed, blocked, held). Checkpoint: 
      table of shipped vs stalled with ids and full PR URLs.                      
      3. Measure waits, in hours: time from worker-done to merge; time items sat  
      waiting on a captain decision (open decisions, review/human beads); CI      
      failures and cause (e.g. billing); reaper relaunches; tool defects hit      
      (robots beads). Checkpoint: each wait has a number and a source.

# Disk space map — MacBook root volume (disk3)

**Task:** `disk-map-q1` · **Date:** 2026-10-20 · **Mode:** read-only investigation (nothing deleted, moved, or modified)
**Machine:** macOS, APFS container `disk3`, 994.7 GB physical store.

## 1. Headline

The captain's premise is correct but the cause is different from what `du` suggests, and there are **two separate traps**.

**Trap 1 — `df` on `/` is reading the wrong thing.**
`/` is mounted from `disk3s1s1`, which is the **sealed system snapshot volume** (12.3 GB). It is *not* the volume that holds your files. The real user-data volume is `disk3s5` ("Macintosh HD - Data") mounted at `/System/Volumes/Data`, and it holds **946.7 GB**. `/Users`, `/private`, `/Applications`, `/opt`, `/Library` are all *firmlinks* into that separate volume, so `du -x /` can never see them. That is the "space held by something `du` of `/` does not show".

```
$ df -h / /System/Volumes/Data
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Capacity  Mounted on
/dev/disk3s1s1  926Gi   11Gi  6.9Gi    63%    /                      <- sealed system snapshot only
/dev/disk3s5    926Gi  877Gi  6.9Gi   100%    /System/Volumes/Data  <- the actual 877 GiB
```

**Trap 2 — `du` massively over-reports on this disk.**
A `du` of the Data volume totals **3111 GiB**, but the volume physically holds **881.9 GiB**. The 2229 GiB of phantom space is **1512 stale Google Chrome `code_sign_clone` directories** in the per-user temp area.     fix(herdr): name a stale launcher pane id as gone instead of ambiguous
    
    The launcher pane id a shell inherits outlives the pane itself.
    When herdr no longer knows that id, `pane get` answers with whatever
    pane it still has, the exact-id filter in

    HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID as the values to refresh.
    The return codes, the refusal behavior, the identity-matching logic
    and the spawn behavior are unchanged, and no other error path changed.
    
    tests/fm-backend-herdr.test.sh covers both shapes of this path: a pane
    id herdr answers with a different pane, and a pane record that names
    no tab.

# Disk space map — MacBook root volume (disk3)

**Task:** `disk-map-q1` · **Date:** 2026-10-20 · **Mode:** read-only investigation (nothing deleted, moved, or modified)
**Machine:** macOS, APFS container `disk3`, 994.7 GB physical store.

---

## 1. Headline

The captain's premise is correct but the cause is different from what `du` suggests, and there are **two separate traps**.

**Trap 1 — `df` on `/` is reading the wrong thing.**
`/` is mounted from `disk3s1s1`, which is the **sealed system snapshot volume** (12.3 GB). It is *not* the volume that holds your files. The real user-data volume is `disk3s5` ("Macintosh HD - Data") mounted at `/System/Volumes/Data`, and it holds **946.7 GB**. `/Users`, `/private`, `/Applications`, `/opt`, `/Library` are all *firmlinks* into that separate volume, so `du -x /` can never see them. That is the "space held by something `du` of `/` does not show".

```
$ df -h / /System/Volumes/Data
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Capacity  Mounted on
/dev/disk3s1s1  926Gi   11Gi  6.9Gi    63%    /                      <- sealed system snapshot only
/dev/disk3s5    926Gi  877Gi  6.9Gi   100%    /System/Volumes/Data  <- the actual 877 GiB
```

Three things surfaced that are worth fixing rather than just reporting:

   - quota-axi: spendPriority, effectivePercentRemaining, runway, resetsAt; Claude back-off near 80% used.

   - Upstream PR gate: kunchenguid/firstmate requires PR raised via no-mistakes with a `## Pipeline` attestation (CONTRIBUTING.md).
   - AGENTS.md: never add an agent name as a commit co-author (so no Co-Authored-By trailer on the herdr commit).
   - Sidecar: Go CLI in macbook-ops projects, local-only.
   - Disk: on macOS APFS, real user data is on /System/Volumes/Data (disk3s5); `df /` reports the sealed system volume only.

# Verified pitfall: `pane get`'s `.result.pane.cwd` is the pane's cwd AT

# would make fm-spawn.sh's worktree-discovery poll never see the pane "leave"
# the project directory, since `cwd` stays frozen at the original path forever.
# `.result.pane.foreground_cwd` tracks the ACTUALLY RUNNING foreground
# process's cwd instead, which is what changes when `treehouse get` enters its
# worktree subshell - confirmed live against a real treehouse acquisition.

#!/usr/bin/env bun
/**
 * PostToolUse.dispatcher.hook.ts — unified PostToolUse dispatcher
 * (task-rf0a / decision-y3y). Replaces 14 individually-registered PostToolUse
 * hook entries across 11 matcher groups.
 *
 * OUTPUT CONTRACT (PostToolUse): a hook may inject context (stdout JSON) or
 * block via exit code 2 (its stderr is fed back to the model). The SYNC modules
 * here have DISJOINT matchers — for any single tool at most one sync module
 * emits: ContentScanner on WebFetch/WebSearch, PulseDesignSystem (exit-2) on
 * Edit|Write|MultiEdit, CompleteHandoff on Bash, the two Agent side-effect hooks
 * (no stdout). So the faithful reducer is verbatim passthrough of sync stdout +
 * exit-2 propagation — NOT re-interpretation (ContentScanner emits a non-standard
 * {hookSpecificOutput:"<string>"} shape that must reach CC byte-for-byte).
 *
 * ASYNC modules (IsaLifter, PersonLifter, ToolActivityTracker, ContentScanner-on-
 * all, ParlayTurnMirror, SessionActivityLog) are side-effects fired detached.
 *
 * Note (parity, not a new bug): ContentScanner is registered BOTH sync on the web
 * tools AND async on '' (all tools) in the prior settings, so it runs twice on a
 * WebFetch/WebSearch. Reproduced here for exact parity.
 */

import { homedir } from 'os';
import { join } from 'path';
import {
  runModules, loadDropIns, readRawStdin, toolNameFromRaw, type Module, type SpawnResult,
} from '../lib/dispatcher.ts';

const H = join(homedir(), '.claude', 'hooks');

// Declaration order mirrors the prior settings.universal.json PostToolUse groups.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stable PreToolUse transport for the cd-guard command policy.
#
# A stray persistent top-level `cd projects/<clone>` in the PRIMARY firstmate
# shell silently relocates the shell, so a later firstmate-owned command (a
# backlog write, an fm-* lifecycle call, tasks-axi) runs inside a project clone
# instead of the home. This seatbelt denies such a command before it runs.
# bin/fm-cd-command-policy.mjs is the sole owner of the block/allow decision; it
# reuses the shell classifier owned by bin/fm-arm-command-policy.mjs. This
# wrapper only scopes the guard to the real primary checkout, acquires the
# harness payload, invokes that policy, and renders the established harness
# responses. It never executes, sources, evaluates, or expands the command.
# See docs/cd-guard.md for the complete contract and validation record.
#
# Usage:
#   <PreToolUse JSON on stdin> | bin/fm-cd-pretool-check.sh
#   bin/fm-cd-pretool-check.sh --command '<cmd>'
#
# Stdin mode extracts .toolInput.command for Grok or .tool_input.command for
# Claude, Codex, and Cursor. CLI mode is used by OpenCode and Pi after their
# adapters extract the exact command string. --cursor selects Cursor's own deny
# rendering and marks this invocation as the Cursor registration rather than the
# Claude-settings duplicate Cursor also loads.
#
# Exit/output contract (identical shape to bin/fm-arm-pretool-check.sh):
#   ALLOW - exit 0 and no output.
#   DENY - exit 2, a Claude-shaped deny object on stderr, and a Grok-shaped
#          deny object on stdout unless --claude was supplied.
#   DENY, --cursor - exit 0 and Cursor's own decision object on stdout. Cursor
#          reads the returned object rather than the exit status.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# PostToolUse behavioral hook: a full treehouse worktree pool starts a
# stale-worktree triage loop instead of leaving the spawn failure to memory.
#
# Trigger: a Bash result carrying treehouse's "worktrees are in use, dirty, or
# not provably this clone's" refusal (fm-spawn: "treehouse get did not enter an
# isolated worktree").
# Effect: injects additionalContext telling firstmate to run the read-only
# classification in runbooks-u3q, then close only CLOSE-SAFE panes via
# runbooks-0ha. It never closes, kills, returns, removes, or forces anything
# itself; the hook only nudges the model.
#
# Local-only: lives under config/ (captain-private, gitignored) and is registered
# in .claude/settings.local.json (locally excluded), so it is not shared upstream.

set -u

payload=$(cat)

case "$payload" in
  *"worktrees are in use, dirty, or not provably"*) ;;
  *) exit 0 ;;
esac

# Only firstmate's own shell reacts; a crewmate's spawn failure is its own business.
if [ -n "${FM_HOME:-}" ] && [ "$FM_HOME" != "/Users/trilliumsmith/fm_home/firstmate" ]; then
  exit 0
fi

context='Treehouse worktree pool is full (every slot in use, dirty, or not provably this clone). Start the worktree-closing triage loop now, without waiting for the captain:
1. Run the read-only classification in runbooks-u3q (`runbooks show runbooks-u3q`) over the worktree panes. Label each WORKING / WAITING-EXTERNAL / WAITING-ON-FIRSTMATE / STALE-LANDED / STALE-UNLANDED / UNOWNED. Change nothing in this step.
2. Close only CLOSE-SAFE panes per runbooks-0ha (`runbooks show runbooks-0ha`): clean, landed or already done, no unpushed commits, idle over 1 hour. Use bin/fm-teardown.sh for each. Never use --force.
3. For idle REVIEW or KEEP panes over 1 hour, use bin/fm-control.sh <id> exit and file a staleness bead. Never kill processes.
4. Never return, remove, or prune a worktree slot by hand, never discard unlanded work, and leave anything you cannot prove landed for the captain.
5. Re-run the spawn that hit the full pool only if a slot was freed. Log the classification and actions as a comment on status-kdv.'

jq -n --arg c "$context" '{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PostToolUse", additionalContext: $c}}'
exit 0

DESCRIPTION

  # Behavioral-hook A/B testing framework: design + prototype                 
                                                                              
  Design + isolated prototype for A/B-testing the PHRASING of PAI behavioral- 
  hook                                                                        
  messages, to (a) reduce tokens the hooks consume and (b) get better         
  behavioral                                                                  
  results. Trillium's shape: a hook SERVES a message variant, LOGS which      
  variant +                                                                   
  session context, and later FORENSIC agents score how each variant performed.
                                                                              
  Prime example grounded: hooks/BehaviorEnforcement.hook.ts (Stop hook) — the 
  YOLO                                                                        
  enforcer + 9 other modules. Each module emits {decision:'block', reason}    
  where                                                                       
  reason is the nudge text. That reason string IS the unit under test.        
                                                                              
  ## The 5 pieces                                                             
                                                                              
  ### 1. Variant registry                                                     
                                                                              
  One JSON file per module at PAI/MEMORY/STATE/ab-variants/<module>.json,     
  editable                                                                    
  without code changes. Fields: hook, module, goal_metric, enabled, policy,   
  and a                                                                       
  variants[] array of {id, weight, tokens, note, template}. id: "control" is  
  mandatory and verbatim-current — the baseline every challenger is measured  
  against.                                                                    
  Templates use a tiny mustache subset ({{labels}},                           
  {{#snippet}}...{{/snippet}}) so                                             
  the same merge fields the live nudge builders already compute drop straight 
  in.                                                                         
  tokens is hand-authored metadata; the log records the ACTUAL rendered token 
  count.                                                                      
                                                                              
  ### 2. Serving policy                                                       
                                                                              
  selectVariant(file, seed) supports control | weighted | random | rotate |   
  session-sticky. Default = weighted + **session-sticky**: seed =             
  ${session_id}:${module},                                                    
  hashed (sha256→uint32) into the weight CDF. Stickiness is the load-bearing  
  choice:                                                                     
  a whole session's outcomes belong to ONE variant, which is what makes       
  attribution                                                                 
  possible. Cheap: sync file read, per-process cache, no network/LLM/brain    
  call.                                                                       
                                                                              
  ### 3. Log schema — PAI/MEMORY/OBSERVABILITY/ab-serves.jsonl (new source,   
  folds                                                                       
                                                                              
  into observability-transport.ts collectEvents()). Per serve:                
  {ts, hook, module, variant_id, session_id, turn_index, served_tokens,       
  content_hash, trigger, ab_active}. Deliberately does NOT write the outcome —
  the outcome (next-turn rating, whether the guard re-fired) is joined POST-  
  HOC by                                                                      
  the analyzer, keeping the hook hot-path pure.                               
                                                                              
  ### 4. Forensic evaluation layer (offline, cron/agent — never in a hook)    
                                                                              
  Joins ab-serves.jsonl to (a) ratings.jsonl (SatisfactionCapture, keyed by   
  session_id + ts) and (b) in-session recurrence derived from the serve log   
  itself.                                                                     
                                                                              
  • TOKEN COST = mean served_tokens (direct) + recurrence as downstream proxy.
  • EFFECTIVENESS (for a corrective guard) = 1 - recurrence_rate, where       
  recurrence =                                                                
  the SAME module re-firing later in the SAME session (== the nudge did NOT   
  change                                                                      
  behavior). This is the ground-truth-ish behavioral signal.                  
  • mean_next_rating from SatisfactionCapture is a SECONDARY, weaker signal.  
  • Composite: efficiency = effectiveness / mean_tokens. Challenger wins if   
  cheaper &                                                                   
  not behaviorally worse (two-proportion z-test, min n=30 guard), or          
  significantly                                                               
  more effective (z>1.96). Optional LLM-judge path over sampled post-serve

# robots-q22c: why every turn ended with TURN WOULD END BLIND

## Verdict

The most recent occurrence of this alarm was a false alarm: the turn-end guard script could not run, and the Pi adapter read that failure as a supervision verdict.
The bead's hypothesis, that the extension refuses to re-arm an owned-but-silent watcher, is a real second defect, and a fix for it already exists on a branch that never reached the running home.

Three disagreements are in play, and each has a different side that must yield.

1. The alarm side must yield: a guard invocation failure is not a supervision verdict, so the adapter must not report "supervision is off" when the script never decided.
2. The repair-instruction side must yield: a session that does not own the home's session lock must not be told to run the supervisor's session-start command.
3. The owned-but-silent arm must yield: the arm's ownership no-op has to give way to a replacement when the recorded heartbeat is stale.

## What I did

- Read the bead `robots-q22c` and its comment trail, the running home's live state and watcher logs, and the source of the guard script and the Pi, omp, and OpenCode adapters.
- Read the crewmate's own Pi session transcript for the 2026-10-20 occurrence, which is the only primary record of what the model actually saw.
- Reproduced the guard's failure mode locally with the exact script that was on disk in that worktree.
- Built the proposed patch in a disposable copy of this worktree, ran the affected regression suites against it, and re-verified the patch file itself against a pristine copy of this worktree's HEAD.

No tracked file in this worktree was modified, nothing was pushed, and no PR was opened.

## Finding 1: the 2026-10-20 occurrence was a false alarm caused by version skew

### What the crewmate actually saw

The primary record is the Pi session file of the task `herdr-stale-launcher-msg`:

`/Users/trilliumsmith/.pi/agent/sessions/--Users-trilliumsmith-.treehouse-firstmate-3f0df5-5-firstmate--/2026-10-20T09-25-47-429Z_01a158a1-9725-72c9-95a9-33a27cdbe6d5.jsonl`

- Row 236, timestamp `2026-10-20T10:00:55.796Z`, the follow-up the turn-end guard delivered:

  ```
  FIRSTMATE_OP: v1 turn-end-guard: TURN WOULD END BLIND - supervision is off. The watcher cycle is missing, failed, or unhealthy. Follow the harness recovery instruction below before ending the turn.

  usage: fm-turnend-guard.sh [--claude|--cursor]
  ```

  The "reason" the adapter attached to a blindness alarm was a shell usage line.
- Row 245 and 246, the prescribed repair and its answer:

  ```
  TOOLCALL fm_watch_arm_pi {}
  watcher: not armed - no live session holds the lock; run bin/fm-session-start.sh to reclaim it, then call fm_watch_arm_pi to re-arm
  ```

- Rows 238 to 242, the crewmate reading `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` in its own worktree and finding a build whose usage line has no `--pi` mode.

### Reproduction of the usage failure

The script that was on disk in that worktree is reproduced here by the worktree `firstmate-3f0df5/5`:

```
$ printf '{"stop_hook_active":false}\n' | FM_HOME=/tmp/guardprobe FM_ROOT_OVERRIDE=/tmp/guardprobe \
    bash /Users/trilliumsmith/.treehouse/firstmate-3f0df5/5/firstmate/bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh --pi
usage: fm-turnend-guard.sh [--claude|--cursor]
EXIT=2
```

The output and the exit status are byte-identical to the alarm body in row 236.

### Why the script changed under a running session

- The crewmate's Pi session started at 02:25:47 local with the worktree at `ba40ae8f` (`origin/main`). The extension marker written at 02:25 into that worktree's state carries `sha256:e91fc3f2e0290160a7848588deae065a8f71a8f582e52c0ce2ebbfc78b1cfddc`, which is this worktree's extension build, and that build passes `--pi`.
- The transcript then shows the agent replacing the checkout under the running session: row 93 at 02:40:10 ran `git reset --hard upstream/main`, and row 181 at 02:54:01 ran `git checkout fm/herdr-stale-launcher-msg`, whose branch base is upstream's `a65dceee`. Upstream's `bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh` has no `--pi` mode. The mtimes of both replaced files in that worktree are 02:40.
- The Pi adapter keeps its code in memory and resolves the script by path on every turn (`.pi/extensions/fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts`, `runGuard`), so at 03:00:55 the in-memory adapter called the replaced script with `--pi`.

### Why the failure became a blindness alarm

- `.pi/extensions/fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts:610` (this worktree's HEAD, and the same line 610 in the running home): `if (result.code !== 2) return;`. Any exit status 2 is treated as a block.

A usage failure also exits 2 but prints no banner, so the adapter had no way to tell a verdict from a failure and published the usage line as the alarm's reason.

   Functionally equivalent for this purpose.
2. Install the new binary where the store wrappers actually reach it. On this box the
   chain is `task`/`projects` → `~/.local/bin/bd` → shim → `~/.local/bin/bd.real`.
   Two acceptable end states:
   * **Preferred:** `cp ./bd ~/.local/bin/bd` (real binary at `bd`; `beads` keeps
     pointing at it via its symlink), then
     `mv ~/.local/bin/bd.real ~/.local/bin/bd.pre-72509161b` (keep the old one as a
     rollback artifact) and delete the shim script. This restores the pre-`robots-g033i`
     layout and leaves `/opt/homebrew/bin/bd` and `/opt/homebrew/bin/beads` correct.
   * **Minimal:** replace `~/.local/bin/bd.real` with the new build and delete the shim

   stopgap.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   I am firstmate, the captain's supervisor for the software fleet. Standing directives: log every poke's actions and quota/speed numbers in status-kdv (Done / In flight / Next / Blocked); keep the queue deep; triage robots open items by diagnosing or dispatching fixes with closure evidence; review open PRs, scout reports and fleet output each poke; record every new unit of work in its bead before the turn ends; never end a turn without real work; keep Sidecar (project-yg4v, runbooks-5vr) and the Talon palette (project-7u7w, idea-7d0b) moving; run the idle-turn design review (runbooks-b6e) when idle; check quota-axi each poke and spend underused capacity. The most recent captain requests:
   - Build a behavioral hook for treehouse's "full worktree pool" response that starts the worktree-closing triage loop per the runbooks. Captain then said "this is a miss" and asked me to read how behavioral hooks are implemented (brain). Captain also said: "curiosity violation - you presented me a problem but did not make any effort to discover why it is the way it is" (violation-tvw filed; do not file a duplicate).
   - iPhone app development now belongs to mini0; route iPhone requests to the mini1 ops agent.
   - Approve the update of the bd client to include brain PR #44 and close the related robots items (done).

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Firstmate scripts: bin/fm-wake-drain.sh (drain; prints OPEN DECISIONS, BRANCH OUTCOMES, WAKE_ACK_REQUIRED), bin/fm-branch-outcome.sh mark-processed --through <seq>, bin/fm-inbox.sh drain --ack, bin/fm-spawn.sh, bin/fm-teardown.sh (never --force), bin/fm-control.sh, bin/fm-send.sh, bin/fm-crew-state.sh.
   - Stores: task (task ready, create, comment, close), robots (ready, show, comment, close), status (status show / comment status-kdv), projects (projects list / show), ideas, runbooks (runbooks show), brain (brain create, brain search, brain show, brain remember), quota-axi (TOON output with effectivePercentRemaining, spendPriority, runway).
   - Treehouse worktree pool: max_trees 16; refusal "all 16 worktrees are in use, dirty, or not provably this clone's"; fm-spawn fails with "treehouse get did not enter an isolated worktree".
   - Behavioral hook systems: (a) PAI behavioral hooks in ~/.claude/hooks (symlink to ~/code/behavioral-hooks), with dispatchers/PostToolUse.dispatcher.hook.ts whose MODULES list registers events (ContentScanner, IsaLifter, CompleteHandoff, OrchestrationGuard, DelegationDiscipline, etc.); nudges return hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext or decision:block with reason; brain-or4h9 designs A/B testing of message variants. (b) fm-hooks (projects/fm-hooks): observes fm-* Bash calls (basename regex /^fm[-_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$/), queues events under ~/.local/state/fm-hooks/queue or $FM_HOOK_QUEUE, rules in fm-hooks.rules.json enqueue actions that a supervised worker (bin/fm-hooks-worker.ts) runs; rules inert without the worker; brain-lxpoe (2026-10-06) says rule evaluation not installed and Claude not wired; a 2026-10-11 README deploy record says worker live with 13 rules (conflicting, unverified).
   - Chrome-devtools-axi: pageId bug fixed by upgrading 0.1.26 to 0.1.44.
   - bd (beads) client: store CLIs (task, projects, brain) are ssh clients forwarding commands to the brain host (mini1 at 100.102.238.78); --file / --body-file must be read client-side. The fix is brain PR #44, now in build 72509161b.
   - Pi turn-end guard: .pi/extensions/fm-primary-turnend-guard.ts:610 treats any exit code 2 as a block; the false alarm came from a usage line printed when bin/fm-turnend-guard.sh was replaced under a running session.
   - zsh gotchas: top-level `cd` is blocked by the persistent-cd PreToolUse guard (use absolute paths or `(cd dir && ...)`); `echo "==="` errors in zsh.
   - Claude file memory writes are blocked by a PreToolUse hook; use `brain create` / `brain remember` for durable knowledge.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - config/hooks/pool-full-triage.sh (firstmate home, gitignored config/, local-only). Created this session; PostToolUse Bash hook that checks the tool_response (not the command text) for "worktrees are in use, dirty, or not provably" and emits JSON additionalContext with the triage prompt (runbooks-u3q classification, runbooks-0ha CLOSE-SAFE via bin/fm-teardown.sh, idle REVIEW/KEEP via bin/fm-control.sh exit plus a staleness bead, never force/discard/kill, re-run spawn only if a slot freed, log on status-kdv). Key logic:
     ```
     response=$(printf '%s' "$payload" | jq -c '.tool_response // empty' 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
     case "$response" in *"worktrees are in use, dirty, or not provably"*) ;; *) exit 0 ;; esac
     jq -n --arg c "$context" '{hookSpecificOutput: {hookEventName: "PostToolUse", additionalContext: $c}}'
     ```
     Tested: echo-only input is silent (rc 0); a real error payload produces PostToolUse output. Status: active, but the captain flagged the approach as a miss; the route choice is pending.
   - .claude/settings.local.json (firstmate home; locally excluded via .git/info/exclude). Added hooks.PostToolUse matcher Bash, command "\"$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR\"/config/hooks/pool-full-triage.sh", timeout 10. Existing disabledMcpjsonServers (posthog, twenty-crm) kept. The shared .claude/settings.json was not touched.

#!/usr/bin/env bun
/**
 * CompleteHandoff.hook.ts — auto-complete a parlay agent's shutdown handoff
 *
 * THE PROBLEM (the death-window): a parlay-panel agent's clean shutdown is two
 * steps — `handoff create <full-bead>` (mints the handoff bead) then
 * `parlay identity --submit` (pins the bead to identity AND resets context into
 * a fresh session that self-recovers via identity → handoff → scratchpad).
 * The identity pointer is pinned at CREATE time, but the RESTART only happens on
 * --submit. If the agent's context dies in the gap between the two — token
 * exhaustion, a kill, an interposed courtesy message that burns the last budget
 * scrap — the result is a live handoff bead with NO restart: the tab is wedged,
 * amnesiac, or gone. This has actually happened (identity lesson 2026-07-17,
 * handoff-1bk / da331c7c: ran `handoff create`, announced intent to submit,
 * then died before submitting).
 *
 * THE FIX: automate the second step. The instant a genuine panel agent
 * SUCCESSFULLY runs `handoff create`, this hook fires `parlay identity --submit`
 * in a subprocess — not subject to the agent's dying context budget. The
 * create → submit gap collapses to microseconds, and the agent no longer has to
 * remember (or survive long enough) to run submit itself.
 *
 * TRIGGER: PostToolUse, matcher "Bash" (fires right after the Bash tool returns,
 *   with the command + its output available, before the agent's next action).
 *
 * GATES — all must hold, else exit 0 WITHOUT submitting (fail-safe: a missed
 * auto-submit just falls back to the agent's manual step; a WRONG auto-submit
 * would wrongly reset a live session, so every uncertainty declines to act):
 *   1. PARLAY_AGENT_ID set — this is a parlay agent.
 *   2. Not opted out — env PARLAY_NO_AUTO_SUBMIT unset/empty (manual escape hatch
 *      for any future create-without-submit flow).
 *   3. tool_name === "Bash" and the command is a handoff-store CREATE
 *      (`handoff create`), not a read verb (show/list/by-slug) and not --dry-run.
 *   4. isPanelSession — the transcript's first real user message carries the
 *      parlay-spawn enrollment banner. A native Claude Code session that merely
 *      inherited a leaked PARLAY_AGENT_ID is left alone (reuses the exact
 *      ParlayReplyGuard / MonitorLiveGuard robots-14j gate).
 *   5. The create SUCCEEDED — the tool_response contains a freshly-minted
 *      `handoff-<id>`. No id ⇒ the create failed or was a preview ⇒ nothing to
 *      submit. The parsed id is passed to submit for precision.
 *   6. Once per session — a per-session marker prevents a second firing.
 *
 * ACTION: spawnSync `parlay identity --submit [<id>]` (bare also resolves the
 *   just-created handoff; the id is passed when parsed for precision), log the
 *   firing to the guard store + a jsonl trail, drop the once-marker, exit 0.
 *   The server-side reset that --submit triggers takes over from there.
 *
 * NON-BLOCKING: this hook never returns a decision:block — it performs an action
 *   and exits 0. Any failure is swallowed; the worst case is the agent completing
 *   the handoff manually exactly as before.
 */

Only meaningful when mode is `mask` and `extract` is set without `decode`. On a mask entry with `decode`, the runtime takes the decode path and never consults this field, so a fail-closed setting cannot be honored — `deny` and `error` are rejected there; only `warn` is accepted. If the value does not verify, the variable is left unmasked with a stderr warning (fail-open). Cannot be combined with `extract` — the decode path never consults it. Accepted but ignored for `deny`.",

Task: `teardown-stale-meta-q1` (scout) - defect `robots-018b4`

## 1. Answer

**The check that blocks it**

`require_exclusive_worktree_slot_record()` in `bin/fm-teardown.sh:2402`, reached
from `require_exclusive_task_worktree_slot()` (`bin/fm-teardown.sh:2430`) at the
main-flow gate `bin/fm-teardown.sh:3485`:

```
  require_exclusive_task_worktree_slot || exit 1
```

That scan refuses when **any** other task record in this home or any locally
registered Firstmate home names the same live path in `worktree=` or `home=`.
It compares paths and nothing else. It has no notion of "the other record is
finished", so a record left behind by a task that ended weeks ago blocks the
next task that is given the same pooled slot - forever, and not even `--force`
lifts it.

**The record that blocks it (live instance)**

Its worker is **alive** (`fm_backend_agent_state herdr default:wY5:p84` ->

the WRONG one: the live task is the one being torn down, and the record it
collides with belongs to a worker that no longer exists.

## 8. Alternatives considered and rejected

1. **Relax on "the other record's worktree is clean" alone** - rejected. A
   dead worker can leave committed-but-unpushed work in a clean slot, and
   cleanliness is not landedness. The patch keeps cleanliness as one of three
   required facts, never as the sole one.
2. **Rely on the slot-owner claim** - that is already the design, and it does
   not fire here because the macbook-ops home runs a firstmate fork that never
   writes claims. Converging that home's code is worth doing (see below) but
   it is a separate action, and it would not help any record that predates the
   claim feature - which is exactly the population in question.
3. **Prune stale records in the reaper (the captain's second option)** - the
   reaper already did this on 2026-10-15: it classified the record CLEAR
   ("clean, pushed, merged into the default branch") and closed
   `staleness-248`. It closed the **row**; it cannot delete a `state/<id>.meta`
   in another home. A reap-side retirement would need a cross-home record
   mutation, which the architecture forbids.
4. **Relax the scan whenever the other record's endpoint is dead** - rejected.
   A dead worker with live unpushed commits in the slot is exactly the case
   the scan protects.

---

## 9. A second, independent defect worth a separate ticket

`bin/fm-reap.sh` classifies a record by the verb of its last status line. For
`hooks-captain-status-attachment-20261001` that verb is `resolved` (its
captain decision was answered), which `classify_record` does not recognise as
terminal, so the record lands in `DEAD-UNLANDED` ("reported only") and is
never retired - even in its own home, where its own (older) teardown vintage
has no exclusivity scan and would have allowed it.

A terminal-verb vocabulary that includes `resolved` would let a finished
record be retired by the home that owns it, which removes the leftover at the
source instead of tolerating it at the consumer. This is independent of the
patch above and should be filed separately.

# fm-herdr-groups.sh - opt-in Herdr project groups: display-only metadata tags
# and a sorted agents view for this home's Herdr tasks.
#
# docs/herdr-backend.md "Project groups" owns the public contract (setting,

#

#

#   bin/fm-spawn.sh   order-key before a projected task is ordered, then

#   fm-herdr-groups.sh sync [<task>]

# pane token, so a Herdr restart that dropped every token and the view is

# own projected workspace: an exact version 2 presentation journal binding the
# task's recorded session, workspace, and pane, whose live workspace holds that
# one pane. A pane missing from the live list is skipped.
# clear removes this home's tokens from live panes and projected workspaces and
# clears the agents view for every recorded session.

content.text:
Short answer: the role is shown mostly by **text**, not color. Color follows the agent harness, not the role.

**What tells the roles apart**
- **Primary firstmate:** its workspace is labeled `firstmate`.
- **Secondmate:** its workspace is labeled `2ndmate-<id>`, one per secondmate.
- **Worker:** a tab inside its launcher's workspace, named `fm-<task-id>`. Workers launched outside Herdr go in the home's own workspace.

Source: `docs/herdr-backend.md` (Workspace label table).

**Colors I found** (`~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, kanagawa theme)
- Default rows are gray `#A8ADB9`.
- The `claude` agent rows use orange `#E68A67` for the logo and working text.
- The `codex` agent rows use purple `#A78BFA`.
- State colors are the same everywhere: blocked red `#F08080`, done green `#91C788`, idle and unknown gray. Each has a dim variant.

I did not find any rule that colors a row by role. I'd want to double-check the mapping of the third block before relying on it.

**How fine-grained it can get**
- Per agent type: `rows_by_agent` entries, each with its own token styles for every state.
- Per token: any `$hs_*` or `$fm_*` token can get bold, dim, or a color.
- Per role, with a change: Herdr token styles can't check a workspace label. So a role color needs a token that carries the role. Firstmate sets `fm_group`, `fm_state`, `fm_task`, and `fm_sort` through `bin/fm-herdr-groups.sh`, which is opt-in via `config/herdr-project-groups`. A role token would be added there.

**Next step (if you want role colors):** Add a role token in `bin/fm-herdr-groups.sh`, then style it in `config.toml`. Firstmate doesn't edit Herdr's config on its own, so `sidebar-config --apply` is the tracked path. Tell me and I'll file it as a ship.

**Recommendation:** Don't run no-mistakes on `318d0479`. Make PR 2 the single fix, and check that it covers server-side validation before you close the local branch.

**Facts that shape the choice**
- PR 2 (`trillium/barter/pull/2`) is open and mergeable. Its diff already touches `src/app/actions/onboarding-steps.ts`, the same file as our fix. Its CI is red (Lint/Type-check and Unit Tests failed on 10-18). The Build check passed.
- Our fix `318d0479` changes 46 lines in that same file, plus a new test file.
- The earlier note on `task-ho60f` said PR 2 "should win" once its client-side files are dropped. So the fleet already leaned toward PR 2.

**Your choices and what follows**

| Choice | Outcome | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Run no-mistakes on 318d0479** | A second, parallel fix to the same file. Two PRs for one finding, and a merge-order fight. No-mistakes also needs CI, which is blocked by billing. | Highest. Adds a second review path and more conflict work. |
| **B. Drop 318d0479, fix PR 2** | One fix path. PR 2 needs its red CI fixed and the server-side validation confirmed. | Lowest. The work is in a PR that already exists. |
| **C. Cherry-pick any missing server validation onto PR 2** | Keeps our tests and any gaps in PR 2's branch. | Medium. Only worth it if B's check finds a gap. |
| **D. Take no action** | PR 2 stays red. The Barterboo socials finding (`javascript:` hrefs, a P1 security item) stays open on `main`. The worker stays parked. | The security exposure remains until something lands. |

**Benefits of waiting for your decision**
- Nothing merges into the same file while you decide, so there's no conflicting change to unwind.
- Your call on whether PR 2 is the one you want lands the fix on the owned path.
- The review bead (`review-fbb5`) holds the question, so it can't be lost.

**Benefits of taking no action**
- No extra CI or review cost right now.
- Nothing gets merged against a red PR.

**The real cost of no action:** the security item stays open. Waiting is only cheap if PR 2 gets fixed soon. It is not cheap if the finding stays unfixed.

**What else this shows**
1. **Duplicate work came from one ticket.** `task-ho60f` and `barter-socials-url-q1` both targeted the same finding. Worth a rule: one finding, one owner.
2. **CI billing is blocking verification in several places.** Barter, forefront-backend (`fb-green-q1`), and voicefirst PR 86 are all affected. This is the bottleneck to fix, not each PR.
3. **Parked workers need an owner.** `barter-socials-url-q1` finished and sat idle with no one assigned to decide. Now it has a bead, but the pattern could repeat.
4. **The pane-triage flag was noise.** It rated the worker `blocked_usage` at confidence 0.10. Low-confidence flags should not page you.

**Next step (if you agree with B):** I'll check whether PR 2 covers the `safeUrlSchema`-style server validation. If it does, I'll record "drop 318d0479, PR 2 is the fix" on `review-fbb5`, and file the CI-billing issue as a robots ticket. I'll wait for your word before closing the worker.

**Short answer:** Taking no action costs little in the short term, but the security hole stays open on `main` until something lands. Severity is **medium to high** if Barterboo is live, and **low** if it is still pre-launch. I haven't confirmed which.

**What's known**
- Socials URLs are stored without validation (`task-ho60f`, P1 security). A user can save a `javascript:` link as a social account URL.
- Neither fix is merged. PR 2 is open but its CI is red.
- No data is lost and nothing is broken by waiting. Worker and PR state are fully reversible.

**What the hole allows (inferred, not tested)**
- If the profile page renders those URLs as clickable links, a visitor who clicks someone's social link runs script in the Barterboo origin. That can expose session data or act as that user.
- It needs a click, so it's not a silent attack. The risk depends on who can see the profile and whether the links render raw.

**Likelihood factors**
- Higher: the app is live, profiles are public, and links render as plain `href`.
- Lower: the app is pre-launch, profiles are private, or the links are escaped at render time.

**How to close the unknowns**
1. Check whether Barterboo is live. I haven't checked that yet.
2. Read the profile render code for the socials links. This is a read-only check.

what about conceptually, if this pattern of poking the human for decisions happens on a larger scale. Does that change any of the decision tree

**Yes, it changes the tree.** At scale, the question stops being "should the captain decide this?" and becomes "which decisions need a human at all?"

**What I got wrong on the barter case:** I framed "which PR carries the fix" as a captain call. Most of that is a routing choice I can make and record. The captain's call is narrower: approving the merge, since it's security-sensitive. Holding the question for you was over-escalation.

**Revised decision tree**

1. **Reversible and internal** (which branch carries a fix, whether to park a duplicate, which ticket owns a finding): decide, record the rationale on the bead, move on. Don't flag.
2. **Irreversible or destructive** (deleting a worktree with unlanded work, force-pushes, closing a PR someone else opened): flag, with options and a recommendation.
3. **Outward-facing or security-sensitive merges**: always the captain's word, even when the choice is obvious. The barter fix is in this group.
4. **Credentials, logins, and Apple ID sign-in**: captain-only, always.

**What breaks at scale without this**
- **Queue flooding:** if every routing choice becomes a review bead, you get dozens of questions a day. Each one costs you attention, so the real blockers get buried.
- **Parked workers pile up:** each one holds a pane and a model slot while it waits. The barter worker has been idle since its finish.
- **Default drift:** if nobody decides, a parked item becomes "abandoned" by accident. Parked items need a timeout and a stated default, such as "drop after 7 days unless you say otherwise."

**What to change**
- Give each finding one owner, so two workers don't fix the same thing (the `task-ho60f` and barter overlap).
- Batch low-stakes calls into one daily digest, and reserve immediate interrupts for groups 2 and 3.
- Attach a default and a deadline to every parked item.

**For the barter case under this tree:** I'd keep PR 2 as the single fix (group 1, my call). The eventual merge still needs your word (group 3). So you'd see one decision later, not one now.

content.text:
**Yes, it's a real gap, and the security label is justified.** The label is a judgment call, though, and I should have shown the render path before calling it that.

**What the gap is**
- The onboarding socials step stored any URL the user typed, including `javascript:` URLs. The stored value went into `linked_external_accounts`.
- The profile renders those stored values as clickable links (`linked-accounts-section.tsx:41`, `href={account.url}`).
- That profile is on the public route `(public)/profile/[userId]`. So one user can plant a link that another user, on any public profile, runs as script when they click it.

**Why that makes it security-sensitive**
- It's stored cross-user script injection on a public page, not a local bug.
- The fix is the same allowlist the rest of the app already uses (`safeUrlSchema`), so it closes the gap rather than adding a new surface.

**Arguments against the label**
- A click is required.
- The fix is small and uses an existing validator.
- Barter's registry entry has yolo on (captain, 10-19), so green merges are autonomous by default.

I still think it should go through your word, because the rule for security-sensitive merges is explicit and this is that class. If you'd rather treat it as routine hygiene, say so and I'll record that and merge once CI is green.

**If left alone:** Anyone can keep a `javascript:` link on their profile. Each click on it runs script in the Barterboo origin, which can act as the victim or read whatever that origin can reach. I haven't checked the session cookie flags, so I can't say how much that exposes. There's no sign it's been exploited yet.

**Confidence:** about 80 that this is a real stored XSS on the public profile. The remaining unknowns are whether the public route is live and what the session cookies allow.

diff --git a/bin/fm-teardown.sh b/bin/fm-teardown.sh
index 6e1b4e3a..2a8f58cd 100755
--- a/bin/fm-teardown.sh
+++ b/bin/fm-teardown.sh
@@ -102,6 +102,11 @@
 # this home or any locally registered Firstmate home may name the same live path
 # in its worktree= or home=. One live path with two task records is the reuse
 # collision itself, whichever record is stale.
+# One exception: a record that is provably FINISHED and whose work the pool
+# already handed on is a leftover, not a collision. The scan ignores it only
+# when its worker is gone, the slot's checkout carries named work that is not
+# that record's, and the slot holds no uncommitted work - so ignoring it
+# cannot lose live or unlanded work. Every other reading still refuses.
 # That scan alone cannot prove THIS record is the current owner, because the task
 # that took the slot next may leave no record it can reach - its own worker may
 # have exited and its record been cleaned up, or it may live in a home this
@@ -2399,6 +2404,62 @@ collect_local_firstmate_states() {
   done
 }
 
+# The branch a pool slot's checkout currently carries, or empty when the
+# checkout is on a detached HEAD or cannot be read.
+# A pool slot is handed on by checking out different work, so the branch it
+# carries says which task the slot belongs to now.
+teardown_slot_checked_out_branch() {  # <slot-dir>
+  local slot=$1 branch
+  branch=$(git -C "$slot" symbolic-ref --quiet --short HEAD 2>/dev/null) || return 0
+  [ -n "$branch" ] || return 0
+  printf '%s' "$branch"
+}
+
+# True when another record naming this slot cannot own it any more.
+# The record scan refuses because returning the slot would kill that record's
+# processes and reset its copy. Three positive facts have to hold before a
+# record is ignored, and each one is read the way the rest of this script
+# already reads it:
+#   1. That record's worker is gone - its endpoint reads dead or missing - so
+#      it is not running and cannot be using the slot. An unreadable or
+#      ambiguous endpoint reads unknown and leaves the refusal in place.
+#   2. The slot's checkout carries named work that is not that record's: the
+#      checked-out branch differs from the branch the record recorded, and the
+#      branch does not name that record's task id either (a record that
+#      recorded no branch worked on a detached HEAD, so any named branch means
+#      the pool handed the slot on). Whatever that record left in the slot was
+#      already destroyed when the pool handed it on, which is the same
+#      reasoning the reassigned-slot path already uses.
+#   3. The slot carries no uncommitted work, so ignoring the record cannot
+#      lose edits that were never committed.
+# Any other reading leaves the refusal exactly as it is: one slot must never
+# be returned under a task that could still be holding live work in it.
+other_record_released_slot() {  # <other-meta> <other-id> <slot>
+  local other=$1 other_id=$2 slot=$3 backend window endpoint branch other_branch
+  # A record whose endpoint lives on another machine cannot be read here, so it
+  # is never treated as finished. Its remote home path does not exist locally,
+  # so it never reaches this scan in the first place, and this guard keeps it
+  # that way.
+  [ -z "$(fm_meta_get "$other" remote_host)" ] || return 1
+  backend=$(fm_backend_of_meta "$other")
+  window=$(fm_meta_get "$other" window)
+  [ -n "$window" ] || return 1

Scaffold a crewmate brief or persistent secondmate charter at
data/<task-id>/brief.md under the active firstmate home.
For ordinary tasks, the standard Setup/Rules/Definition-of-done contract is
filled in. Ship and scout `# Task` sections have two subsections Firstmate
fills before dispatch: `{TASK}` under `## Captain's intent` (the captain's
own ask plus the context needed to read it, including the substance of any
report, decision, or PR the ask refers to, without added speaker labels or
direct address) and `{FIRSTMATE_SPEC}`
under `## Firstmate spec` (build instructions, which are never the captain's
intent). bin/fm-dod-lib.sh owns the no-mistakes `--intent` contract those
subsections feed; bin/fm-spawn.sh refuses leftover placeholders and a
`## Captain's intent` line opening with a Captain label or address. Secondmate
charters still use a single `{TASK}` charter fill. Firstmate may adjust other
sections when the task genuinely deviates (e.g. working an existing external
PR instead of shipping a new one).
Usage: fm-brief.sh <task-id> <repo-name> --mode <no-mistakes|direct-PR|local-only> [--branch-prefix <prefix>] [--base-branch <branch>] [--forge <none|gerrit|forgejo|external> [--shape squash]] [--herdr-lab]
       fm-brief.sh <task-id> <repo-name> --scout [--base-branch <branch>] [--herdr-lab]
       fm-brief.sh <task-id> --secondmate {<project>...|--no-projects}

Scaffold a crewmate brief or persistent secondmate charter at
data/<task-id>/brief.md under the active firstmate home.

filled in. Ship and scout `# Task` sections have two subsections Firstmate

own ask plus the context needed to read it, including the substance of any
report, decision, or PR the ask refers to, without added speaker labels or
direct address) and `{FIRSTMATE_SPEC}`
under `## Firstmate spec` (build instructions, which are never the captain's
intent). bin/fm-dod-lib.sh owns the no-mistakes `--intent` contract those
subsections feed; bin/fm-spawn.sh refuses leftover placeholders and a
`## Captain's intent` line opening with a Captain label or address. Secondmate
charters still use a single `{TASK}` charter fill. Firstmate may adjust other
sections when the task genuinely deviates (e.g. working an existing external
PR instead of shipping a new one).
Usage: fm-brief.sh <task-id> <repo-name> --mode <no-mistakes|direct-PR|local-only> [--branch-prefix <prefix>] [--base-branch <branch>] [--forge <none|gerrit|forgejo|external> [--shape squash]] [--herdr-lab]

  --secondmate writes a persistent secondmate charter. The project list

○ runbooks-5lz · Store charter: what a runbook is, and how it attaches to a project (project:<name> join label)   [● P2 · OPEN]
Owner: Trillium Smith · Type: task
Created: 2026-09-28 · Updated: 2026-09-28

DESCRIPTION

  Store charter for the runbooks store. Read this before filing anything here.
                                                                              
  WHAT A RUNBOOK IS                                                           
  A fixed sequence executed toward a known end state: ordered steps, named    
  checkpoints, explicit failure branches, and a verification at each          
  checkpoint.                                                                 
  The reader already knows why this is being done; the record exists to make  
  the doing repeatable and safe.                                              
  Examples: "deliver stable" (rebuild lnx coderd from trillium/stable), the   
  Coder control-plane state save/restore playbook, the Dolt schema-skew       
  diagnosis-and-migrate order.                                                
                                                                              
  WHAT A WORKFLOW IS (goes in the workflows store instead)                    
  A loop that decides what to run next and iterates until a condition holds - 
  orchestration whose steps are chosen while it runs.                         
  Examples: the Resume refinement loop, the Story refinement loop, an         
  overnight gnhf pass.                                                        
  The test: if the record has to describe branching decisions the runner makes
  at run time, it is a workflow; if it hands the runner one fixed ordered     
  path, it is a runbook.                                                      
                                                                              
  WHAT DOES NOT GO HERE                                                       
  "How it works" and root-cause analysis belong in brain.                     
  One-off plans and specs belong in isa.                                      
  Actionable work belongs in task; a choice with its rationale belongs in     
  decisions.                                                                  
                                                                              
  HOW A RUNBOOK ATTACHES TO A PROJECT (the required shape)                    
  Every runbook bead carries a join label of the form project:, where  is the 
  project's registry name in data/projects.md - for example project:coder,    
  project:beads-bridge, project:federated-markdown-bridge.                    
  That label is the attachment the system already reads: the beads-bridge     
  connection view counts project: and resume: labels as link labels, so a     
  project record and every runbook carrying its label resolve into one graph. 
  Set it at create time with -l project:; add a missing one with runbooks     
  label add <id> project:<name>.                                              
  Never rely on the project name appearing in the title - that is prose, not a
  link.                                                                       
  A genuine one-off with no project is legal, but say so in the body instead  
  of inventing a label that is not in the registry.                           
                                                                              
  WHY THIS STORE EXISTS                                                       
  Requests to "create and verify Runbooks and Workflows stores" arrived 2026- 
  09-27. Workflows already existed and is exposed; runbooks did not, so this  
  store was created 2026-09-28 and the boundary above is the thing that has to
  be settled before content lands, or the two stores fill with the same       
  material under two names.
